subject.title: perf: avoid event-loop stall during embedded_run bootstrap-context

question: Is the current direct glob/liveness proof plus focused tests enough to accept the bootstrap-context session-state risk, or should the contributor provide a full connected embedded_run/channel proof before merge?
rationale: The patch is code-review clean, but it changes prompt/bootstrap context loading and hook scheduling on a P1 message-delivery path, and only maintainers can decide the proof bar for that runtime risk.

options.title: Accept after green exact-head CI
options.body: Land once current-head CI is green, accepting the focused real-behavior proof and test coverage as sufficient for this bounded mitigation.

options.title: Require live embedded_run proof
options.body: Ask for a connected gateway/channel run or redacted runtime logs showing the bootstrap-context stall no longer blocks I/O before merge.

options.title: Narrow the branch further
options.body: Ask the author to split diagnostics or lower-confidence glob parity changes if maintainers want only the async read/yielding walker minimum.

recommendation.title: Accept after green exact-head CI
recommendation.body: Land once current-head CI is green, accepting the focused real-behavior proof and test coverage as sufficient for this bounded mitigation.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter is the strongest history owner for the bootstrap read, hook, and bootstrap-file architecture touched by the PR.
